'''Keith Douglas Horne''' {{postnominals|country=GBR|FRSE}} is an American astronomer. He is Emeritus Professor in the School of Physics and Astronomy at the [[University of St Andrews]].<ref name=uniprofile />

Horne completed his undergraduate degree in Mathematics and Physics at [[Pomona College]] in 1977, and earned his doctorate from [[Caltech]] in 1983.<ref name="uniprofile">{{cite web |title=Keith Douglas Horne |url=https://research-portal.st-andrews.ac.uk/en/persons/keith-douglas-horne |website=University of St Andrews Research Portal |publisher=[[University of St Andrews]] |access-date=1 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250123043146/https://research-portal.st-andrews.ac.uk/en/persons/keith-douglas-horne |archive-date=23 January 2025}}</ref> His [[doctoral advisor]] was [[John Beverley Oke]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Keith Douglas Horne |url=https://astrogen.aas.org/front/searchdetails.php?agnumber=6953 |website=AstroGen |publisher=[[American Astronomical Society]] |access-date=1 May 2025}}</ref> In 2010, he was part of an international team that discovered the [[Hot Jupiter]] exoplanet [[Qatar-1b]].<ref>{{cite web |title=International team discovers alien planet that's Jupiter-sized |url=https://insider.si.edu/2010/12/international-team-discovers-new-exoplanet-1-2-times-as-large-as-jupiter/ |website=[[Smithsonian Insider]] |publisher=[[Smithsonian Institution]] |access-date=1 May 2025 |date=14 December 2010}}</ref>

Horne was the 2004 recipient of the [[Herschel Medal]], which he received for his [[observational astronomy]] work on [[cataclysmic variable star]]s.<ref>{{cite news |title=Awards |url=https://www.thetimes.com/uk/politics/article/awards-bkgfnhm6fmj |access-date=1 May 2025 |work=[[The Times]] |date=11 March 2004 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=National prize for St Andrews star-gazer |url=https://news.st-andrews.ac.uk/archive/national-prize-for-st-andrews-star-gazer/ |website=University of St Andrews |access-date=1 May 2025 |date=31 March 2004}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Herschel Medal Winners |url=https://ras.ac.uk/sites/default/files/2020-04/Herschel%20Medal_medallists.pdf |publisher=[[Royal Astronomical Society]] |access-date=1 May 2025 |year=2020}}</ref>
